appraisal_events.evidence: Mais le docteur Cottard, qui n'avait jamais entendu ce calembour, ne le comprit pas et crut à une erreur de M. de Forcheville. Il s'approcha vivement pour la rectifier : « Mais non, ce n'est pas serpent à sonates qu'on dit, c'est serpent à sonnettes », dit-il d'un ton zélé, impatient et triomphant. Forcheville lui expliqua le calembour. Le docteur rougit.
appraisal_events.explanation: Cottard mistakes Forcheville's pun for an error and triumphantly 'corrects' it, only to be shown that he missed the joke entirely; his zealous confidence makes the ensuing blush all the more exposing.

status_effects.explanation: His confident, triumphant attempt to correct Forcheville backfires completely once the pun is explained, a decisive local loss in the exchange.
His pun ultimately lands as a joke at Cottard's expense once explained, leaving him the amused party pressing Cottard to concede its humor.
